planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in average, well-drained garden soil in full sun to partial shade; Campanulata is a compact, RHS Award of Garden Merit cultivar of the classic gracilis x purpurascens hybrid.

directions: Set out container-grown plants in spring into fertile, humus-rich, well-drained soil, siting in full sun for heaviest bloom or light partial shade in hotter climates. Campanulata forms a dense, rounded dome smothered from June into July in bell-shaped white flowers, each backed by a distinctive purple-flushed calyx and stalk that gives the whole display a soft blush-pink cast against dark green foliage. Prune out a portion of the oldest flowering canes at ground level immediately after bloom to renew the plant and keep flowering wood vigorous. Reliably hardy and low-maintenance once established, it tolerates a range of average garden soils and needs no routine feeding beyond an annual mulch of compost.

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in moist, well-drained soil of any type in full sun for heaviest bloom, though it tolerates partial shade well.

directions: Plant rooted cuttings or container specimens in spring in ordinary, moist but well-drained soil, allowing generous room for its wide-arching, graceful branching habit. Native to mixed forests and mountain valleys of central and southeastern China, Ningpo deutzia produces abundant panicles of small white flowers in June and July on gray-black stems, followed by attractive flaking bark that adds winter interest. This RHS Award of Garden Merit species is one of the larger and more architectural deutzias, well suited as a background shrub or informal screen where its loose, cascading form has space to develop. Renewal-prune after flowering by removing a portion of the oldest canes at the base to maintain vigor and an open, graceful silhouette.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

common_name: Chinese Snow Flower Deutzia (Corymb-Flowered Setchuen Deutzia)

planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun or light, dappled partial shade.

directions: Set out container-grown plants in spring in fertile, humus-rich, well-drained soil, positioning where late spring frosts are less likely to catch the early flush of young growth. Native to forests and mountain thickets of south-central China, this compact species bears broad, branched corymbs crowded with 6 to 50 small, star-shaped white flowers apiece in late spring to early summer, a daintier and more refined effect than the larger racemes of D. scabra or D. gracilis. Slightly hairy young shoots mature into peeling, cinnamon-brown bark on older wood, adding cold-season interest once leaves drop. Prune lightly after flowering to remove spent wood and maintain a graceful, well-branched habit, and mulch in colder parts of its range to protect the root zone.
